bottom_line: In A-HeFT, isosorbide dinitrate plus hydralazine vs placebo improved the primary composite score (−0.1±1.9 vs. −0.5±2.0, P=0.01).
implications: In this trial of 1050 black patients with advanced heart failure on background therapy, the fixed-dose combination improved the primary composite score (−0.1±1.9 vs. −0.5±2.0; P=0.01) and was associated with lower all-cause mortality (6.2% vs. 10.2%) and fewer first heart-failure hospitalizations (16.4% vs. 24.4%), while headache (47.5% vs. 19.2%) and dizziness (29.3% vs. 12.3%) occurred more often with the combination; these data support benefit within the studied population and follow-up as reported.

major_points.text: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in black patients with NYHA class III or IV heart failure with dilated ventricles, on standard therapy.
major_points.quote: The African-American Heart Failure Trial (A-HeFT) was a randomized, placebo-controlled, double- blind trial

major_points.text: The primary end point was a composite score of death from any cause, first hospitalization for heart failure, and change in quality of life at 6 months.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point for the trial was a composite score made up of weighted values for death from any cause, a first hospitalization for heart failure during the 18-month follow-up period, and change in the quality of life at 6 months.

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early due to higher mortality in placebo vs combination therapy.
major_points.quote: The study was terminated early owing to a significantly higher mortality rate in the placebo group than in the group given isosorbide dinitrate plus hydralazine (10.2 percent vs. 6.2 percent, P=0.02).

major_points.text: Primary composite score favored isosorbide dinitrate plus hydralazine vs placebo.
major_points.quote: the primary composite score was ¡0.1±1.9 in the group given isosorbide dinitrate plus hydrala- zine, as compared with ¡0.5±2.0 in the placebo group (P=0.01)

major_points.text: Headache and dizziness were more frequent with combination therapy; CHF exacerbations were more frequent with placebo.
major_points.quote: Symptoms of headache and dizziness were significantly more frequent in the group given isosorbide dinitrate plus hydralazine, whereas exacerbations of congestive heart failure (both moderate and severe) were sig- nificantly more frequent in the placebo group.

absolute_effects.text: Severe exacerbation of CHF: 3.1 percent vs 7.0 percent.
